info.name: Smart Sweep SWMS API
info.description:
Smart Sweep — Solid Waste Management System. Multi-city (City Corporation / Pourashova), with Khulna City Corporation as the pilot.

**Every operation is holding-wise**: the service charge, the monthly bill, payments, the daily collection visit, the QR tag and complaints belong to the holding (the building). Households are occupant records.

Django 5.2 + DRF on PostgreSQL 18. Every endpoint under `/api/`.

## Getting started

1. Start the backend: `cd server && .venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver`
2. Select the **Smart Sweep — Local** environment.
3. Run **00 · Auth → 1 · Request login code**, then **2 · Verify code**. The test scripts capture the JWT pair, the role and the collector id into collection variables, so every other request is authorised automatically.
4. Run **01 · Catalog & setup → Catalog bundle** to see the real ids for cities, wards, tiers and the option lists, then point the `cityId` / `wardId` / `tierId` / `holdingId` variables at them.

## Conventions

- **Auth** — collection-level Bearer `{{accessToken}}`. Access tokens are short-lived; re-run **Refresh access token** when a request answers 401 with `code: "token_invalid"`.
- **Errors** — every failure has one shape: `{"detail": "…", "code": "stable_key", "fields": {"road": ["…"]}}`. `code` is a stable key the UI maps to a translated string.
- **Pagination** — list endpoints return `{count, page, pages, next, previous, results}`. Pass `?page_size=all` for a bare array (capped at 5000).
- **Scoping** — ward, agency and city scoping are applied on the server from the caller's account. They cannot be widened by a query parameter.
- **Ids are text and meaningful** — `HLD-KCC-000001`, `RT-W-14-01`, `C-042` — because field staff read them off building tags.

Interactive schema: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/docs/`

request.description: Does this number have a PIN, and is it locked out? The login screen calls this first to decide whether to offer the PIN fast path or go straight to SMS.

Issues a 4-digit code. The response also carries `known`, `hasPin` and `pinLocked` so the login screen can branch without a second round trip. In DEBUG with `OTP_EXPOSE_CODE=True`, `devCode` holds the code and this request's test script captures it into `{{otpCode}}`.

Throttled under the `otp` scope.

The fast path field collectors use where mobile coverage is unreliable. Returns the same `{access, refresh, user}` body as OTP verification.

An unknown number and a wrong PIN fail identically (`wrong_pin`), so this cannot be used to enumerate accounts. After `PIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` misses the account locks for `PIN_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` and answers `pin_locked`.

request.description: Sets the signed-in operator's PIN. Requires a live access token — a PIN is set *after* an OTP sign-in, never instead of one.
Fails with `no_pin` if none is set, `wrong_pin` if `currentPin` is wrong.
Clears the PIN; the account falls back to OTP-only sign-in.
The session user: role, ward scope, `home` landing route, `readOnly` flag, and the linked `collector` id when the operator is one.
Self-service profile edit. Role and ward scope are **not** writable here — those are set by an agency admin. Returns the full user.
Rotates the refresh token. A dead token answers 401 with `{detail, code: 'token_invalid', fields}` rather than SimpleJWT's own shape, so the frontend interceptor has one envelope to branch on.
Blacklists the refresh token. Always answers `{ok: true}` — revoking an already-dead token is not an error.

request.description:
The Holding Master. **Every operation is holding-wise** — the service charge, the monthly bill, the daily visit and the QR tag belong to the building. Rows carry `qr`, `tier`, `charge`, `paymentMode`, `paymentDay`, read-only `effectiveCharge`, `dues`, `routeId`, `householdCount`, `activeHouseholdCount` and `unitsMatch` (households must equal units; `null` when no unit count is declared).

Ward- and agency-scoped server-side.

The building and the families in it in **one save** — all or nothing. `households` rows without an `id` are created; rows with one update that family; a family left out is untouched (retire one with `status`).

Service terms are the holding's: `tier`, `charge` (0 = the tier's standard), `paymentMode`, `paymentDay`. The QR tag is issued automatically.

**Households must equal units:** more active families than `unitsTotal` is refused (`unitsTotal` error); fewer saves and is flagged by `unitsMatch: false`.
Change the building's service terms. Lowering `unitsTotal` below its active households is refused.
Its bills, payments, visits and complaints cascade with it.

Confirms the building's pin. **This is the gate for routing** — the server refuses to put an unverified holding on a route.

The route planner's to-do list: buildings that could be routed now, and buildings blocked because their location is unverified.

**Admin only.** An `.xlsx` with the upload columns, an example row and a Notes sheet: Holding No · Name · Mobile · City · Ward · Area · Address · Route · GPS Location, plus optional Holding Type · Tier · Charge · Units · Agency.

**Admin only** (agency admin or super admin). Validates every row and returns `{dryRun, rows, summary}` — nothing is written.

Each row reports `action` (`create` | `update`), `status`, `errors` and `warnings`. Checks: required columns and fields; city and ward (code, name or number); mobile `01XXXXXXXXX` (+880 accepted); GPS inside Bangladesh; route in the same ward and only with GPS; tier/agency exist; no duplicate rows; an agency admin uploads only for their own agency.

`Name`/`Mobile` are the owner; `Area` is the road (a new one is added to the ward); GPS pins and verifies the building; a matching ward + area + holding no **updates** instead of duplicating. At most 5000 rows / 5 MB.

**One bill per holding per month.** Rows carry `holding`, `holdingNo`, `head` (the owner), and `received`, `outstanding` and `settlement`, computed from the payments that actually exist.

Filter on **`settlement`**, not `status`: `status` is only ever as fresh as the last `recalculate()`, while `settlement` is derived in SQL and can never disagree with the figures shown.

**Agency admin only.** Returns the same summary as a real run — how many bills, for how much — without writing anything. Answers 200.

Always dry-run first: a run is the only way bills come into existence, and there is no bulk undo.

**Agency admin only.** Issues one bill per **active, routed holding with a charge** (its tier's rate, or its agreed `charge`) for the period and writes a `BillingRun` audit row. Answers 201.

Re-running the same period does not double-charge — existing bills for the month are respected.

item.name: Record a payment against a bill

request.description:
**The only way a bill's status changes.** `Bill.status` is a cache that `recalculate()` derives from the payments that exist, and `Holding.dues` follows from that.

Partial payments are normal — post several and the bill moves unpaid → partial → paid on its own.

Open to **collectors** as well as office roles: the collector at the door is the person the cash is handed to. `collector` defaults to the signed-in collector; leave it out at the office counter, and that difference is what makes the cash reconciliation meaningful.
